query: What recurring issues drive resolution inefficiency?

per_column.name: hardware_device_category
per_column.rationale: Extracts device/asset type from short_description, giving a strong grouping axis to find which categories (e.g., printers) drive recurring inefficiency. Samples map cleanly to source text.

per_column.name: incident_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes failure nature (functionality, connectivity, etc.), a genuine axis for identifying recurring issue types. Sample values are sound readings of the descriptions.

per_column.name: resource_assignment_pattern
per_column.rationale: Single_resolver vs transferred is relevant to resolution inefficiency, but 'transferred' is asserted for 'Printer not working properly' with no evidence of reassignment in the shown fields; this could be inferred from assignment history not present in samples, so groundedness is uncertain.

per_column.name: description_specificity_level
per_column.rationale: Vague/generic descriptions plausibly slow resolution, giving a real axis to correlate with inefficiency. Judgments of specificity from the text are defensible.

per_column.name: issue_scope_impact
per_column.rationale: Scope is useful for prioritizing recurring high-impact issues. But labeling 'The office printer is not functioning' as multi_user_shared_resource and 'Unable to connect to the database' as system_critical are inferences beyond what the terse text states; some are warranted, others speculative.

per_column.name: resolution_path_hint
per_column.rationale: Suggested resolution path is relevant to inefficiency analysis, but values like 'replacement_needed' and 'environmental_trigger' are guesses about remediation not supported by the description text, which only states a symptom.

per_column.name: caller_persistence
per_column.rationale: Repeat reporters are directly relevant to chronic/recurring issues. Derivable by counting caller_id occurrences, an original column, so groundedness is reasonable though not verifiable in the shown samples.

per_column.name: reopened_or_chronic_issue
per_column.rationale: Directly on-point for recurring issues driving inefficiency. However there is no reopen field or state history in the source shown; a true/false chronic flag risks being an unsupported inference, so groundedness is questionable.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide multiple genuine, non-redundant axes (device category, incident type, scope, specificity, persistence, chronicity) that meaningfully support analyzing recurring drivers of resolution inefficiency, so analytical usefulness is strong. Extraction-type columns (hardware_device_category, incident_type) are well grounded in the short_description text. However, several inference-heavy columns (resolution_path_hint, issue_scope_impact, resource_assignment_pattern, reopened_or_chronic_issue) assert specifics the terse source text or shown fields do not clearly support, lowering overall groundedness.
